challenges.title: 24-Hour Care Chains, Exceptional Hours and the 12-Hour Limit

items.title: 12-Hour Limit on 24-Hour Chains
items.text: For 24-hour care chains, Art. 101 applies: if a caregiver works back-to-back shifts for more than 12 hours straight, that is not permitted — hard to track by hand across rotating clients.

items.title: Exceptional Maximum Hours under Art. 106
items.text: In exceptional cases (حالات استثنائية) — such as averting imminent harm, unusual workload pressure, or seasonal peaks — regular working hours may be exceeded, but actual working time may not exceed 10 hours per day or 60 hours per week.

items.title: Overtime Compensated Correctly
items.text: Every overtime hour must be paid at the hourly wage plus 50% of the base wage (effectively 150%) (Art. 107) — since the 2025 reform, optionally as paid time off in lieu.

items.title: Routes Optimised Automatically
items.text: Klacks arranges care visits and routes so that time windows are kept — whether by car or on foot.

items.title: 12-Hour Limit on 24-Hour Chains Blocked
items.text: Klacks automatically prevents shift sequences that would keep a caregiver at the workplace for more than 12 hours straight (Art. 101).

items.title: Exceptional Hours under Art. 106 Tracked
items.text: The exceptional ceiling of 10 hours per day or 60 hours per week is checked continuously, including during seasonal peaks.

items.title: Qualifications Considered Automatically
items.text: Every visit is assigned only to caregivers with the matching qualification.

items.title: On-Premise: Patient Data Stays in KSA
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure. Sensitive biometric time-tracking data stays physically in Saudi Arabia — eliminating the cross-border compliance burden under PDPL/SDAIA.

items.title: Klacksy Schedules by Voice
items.text: "Fill tomorrow’s care routes" is enough. If someone is unavailable, Klacksy immediately suggests an available replacement — without breaching the 12-hour limit.
